detailZh: 伊萨克·哈贾尔确认成为马克斯·维斯塔潘在2027年F1赛季的红牛队友，消息在阿塞拜疆大奖赛前公布。
伊萨克·哈贾尔已与红牛续约一年，将在2027年作为马克斯·维斯塔潘的队友迎来第二个赛季；阿塞拜疆大奖赛周四的练习赛将于上午9:30和下午1点在天空体育 F1直播。
伊萨克·哈贾尔承认他不确定新合同续约的细节，也不确定2027年后是否还会留在红牛，但他希望用驾驶表现来说话。
红牛已确认伊萨克·哈贾尔将在2027年F1赛季继续担任马克斯·维斯塔潘的队友。
哈贾尔在今年年初升入红牛，此前他在2025年代表小红牛完成了令人印象深刻的首个赛季，但由于在上个月夏休期间手腕受伤，他缺席了最近三站比赛。
但这位21岁的车手现在已经恢复到可以驾驶的状态，并将在本周末的阿塞拜疆大奖赛回归，正赛于周六举行——在天空体育 F1直播。

红牛上个月已经宣布，四届世界冠军维斯塔潘签署了一份新合同，至少留在车队至2030年底。
“我们非常兴奋能继续与伊萨克同行。自从今年年初加入我们以来，他在赛道上和赛道外都表现出色，尤其是考虑到这只是他第二个F1赛季，这让续约成为一个容易的决定，”红牛车队领队洛朗·梅基斯说道。
“从一开始，伊萨克就全身心融入车队，在工厂里与工程师们分秒必争地研发赛车，总是渴望学习和进步。
“从墨尔本的第一场比赛周末就能看出，他以非凡的沉着应对了这次跃升，并赢得了这个席位。”
不是双关……续约了！红牛用一段搞笑视频宣布哈贾尔合同！
维斯塔潘身边的第二个红牛席位被广泛认为是F1发车格上最难的位置，此前包括皮埃尔·加斯利、亚历克斯·阿尔本、利亚姆·劳森和角田裕毅在内的多位车手都在与这位荷兰人的较量中陷入困境。
但哈贾尔比这些车手更接近维斯塔潘，本赛季甚至有时胜过队友，因此他的席位并未受到质疑。
尽管缺席了最近三个比赛周末，哈贾尔仍在车手积分榜上排名第八，并在红牛和迈凯伦成功上诉加斯利被推翻的超速处罚后，重新获得了摩纳哥大奖赛的领奖台席位。
伊萨克·哈贾尔在红牛上诉后重新回到摩纳哥领奖台，阿尔派对皮埃尔·加斯利在维修区超速的处罚被恢复表示不满。
“他受伤以来的这段时间对伊萨克来说很艰难，但这次续约证明了我们对他有多么信任，我们迫不及待想看到他在赛道上回归，”梅基斯继续说道。
“本赛季我们还有很多目标要实现，但知道车手、工程师和工厂里的每个人都在朝着同一个方向前进，专注且团结，这种感觉很棒。”
“哈贾尔因为手臂和手腕受伤缺席了最近三站。据我了解，那是他在训练中打重沙袋造成的，因为他在训练中会打拳击。
“但他已经康复，本周末将参赛，并且他将在2027年成为马克斯·维斯塔潘的搭档。
“哈贾尔将继续留在红牛。利亚姆·劳森在他缺席期间替补表现得非常好，但没有人对哈贾尔获得继续留队的认可感到意外。
“他可能是自丹尼尔·里卡多多年前离开以来，维斯塔潘最具竞争力的队友。”
哈贾尔补充道：“我非常兴奋能继续与Oracle红牛车队合作。我在八个月前来到这支车队，立刻明白了这个组织的规模和雄心。
“工厂里有那么多才华横溢的人，你会意识到能为这样一支不可思议的车队效力，与像马克斯这样的四届世界冠军并肩作战，是一种特权。
“从我签约的那一刻起，我就决心为车队奉献自己，在洛朗和米尔顿凯恩斯所有人的支持下，我得以证明他们对我的信任是值得的。我不断寻求倾听、学习，并每天进一步推动自己，思考未来的一切。”
皮埃尔·加斯利和伊萨克·哈贾尔参观太阳马戏团，尝试了一些搞笑的特技！
“如果你足够优秀，就能留下”——哈贾尔谈续约和伤愈复出
周三晚些时候在巴库出席车手新闻发布会时，哈贾尔对媒体表示，他对合同续约谈判完全放松——甚至声称自己不知道合同期限有多长。
“我甚至没有谈过这件事。你知道，我让我的人替我谈，”他说。
“我在赛道上谈[判]，就这样。所以是的，非常容易。”
当被问及是否是多年合同时，哈贾尔回答说：“我其实不知道。我不在乎。是的，但是，你知道，如果你足够优秀，就能留下，就这样。”
这位法国人还谈到了他手腕伤势的性质以及康复过程。
“我的手腕外侧有一处小骨折，这是一个相当漫长的过程，”他说。

Red Bull have confirmed Isack Hadjar will remain as Max Verstappen's team-mate for the 2027 Formula 1 season.

Hadjar stepped up to Red Bull at the start of this year after an impressive debut campaign with Racing Bulls in 2025 but has missed the last three rounds due to a wrist injury he suffered during last month's summer break.
But the 21-year-old is now fit enough to drive and is back at this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, which takes place on Saturday - live on Sky Sports F1.

Red Bull had already announced last month that four-time world champion Verstappen signed a new contract to stay at the team until at least the end of 2030.

"We're very excited to continue our journey with Isack. Since joining us at the start of the year, he has been superb on and off track, especially considering this is only his second Formula 1 season, which made extending his contract an easy decision," said Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies.
"From the very beginning, Isack immersed himself in the team, spending every minute at the factory with his engineers to develop the car, always eager to learn and improve.
"You could see from that first weekend in Melbourne that he handled the step up with remarkable composure and had earned his place in this seat."
No pun… extended! Red Bull announce Hadjar contract in hilarious video!

The second Red Bull seat alongside Verstappen is widely regarded as the toughest on the F1 grid after several drivers including Pierre Gasly, Alex Albon, Liam Lawson and Yuki Tsunoda all struggled against the Dutchman.
But, Hadjar has been closer to Verstappen than those drivers and has even got the better of his team-mate at times this season, so his seat has not come under scrutiny.

Despite missing the last three race weekends, Hadjar is still eighth in the Drivers' Championship and reclaimed his Monaco Grand Prix podium after Red Bull and McLaren successfully appealed Gasly's overturned speeding penalties.

"The period since his injury has been a difficult one for Isack, but this extension is a testament to how much we believe in him and we can't wait to see him back out on track," continued Mekies.

"We still have a lot we want to achieve this season, but it's a great feeling to know that the drivers, engineers and everyone back at the factory are all heading in the same direction, committed and together."
"Hadjar has been out for the last three rounds because he damaged his arm and wrist. I understand that was done by hitting a heavy bag in training because he does boxing in training.
"But he has recovered, he is taking part this weekend, and he will be Max Verstappen's partner in 2027.
"Hadjar will be continuing with Red Bull. Liam Lawson deputised very well in his absence but nobody was surprised that Hadjar gets the nod to carry on.
"He has probably been Verstappen's most competitive teammate since Daniel Ricciardo left a few years ago."
Hadjar added: "I am really excited to continue with Oracle Red Bull Racing. I came to this team eight months ago and immediately understood the scale and ambition of this organisation.
"There are so many talented people at the factory, and you're aware of the privilege of driving for such an incredible team alongside a four-time world champion like Max.

"From the moment I signed, I set out to dedicate myself to the team, and with the support of Laurent and everyone in Milton Keynes, I've been able to justify the faith they've had in me. I'm constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day about what lies ahead."

'If you're good, you stay' - Hadjar on extended deal and injury return

Speaking to the media later on Wednesday in Baku when appearing in the Drivers' Press Conference, Hadjar said he had been completely relaxed about the contract renewal discussions - even claiming he did not know how long the deal was for.
"I didn't even talk about it. You know, I let my people do the talking for me," he said.
"I do it [the talking] on the track and that's about it. So yeah, it was very easy."
And asked whether it was a mufti-year term, Hadjar replied: "I actually don't know. I don't care. Yeah, but, you know, if you're good, you stay, and that's it."
The Frenchman also spoke about the nature of his wrist injury and how his rehabilitation had gone.
"I have a small fracture outside of the wrist and it's just quite a long process," he said.

detailEn: Red Bull has officially retained Isack Hadjar as Max Verstappen's team-mate for the 2027 Formula 1 season.
The team made the announcement upon Hadjar's return from injury at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku, after he'd missed three rounds with a wrist fracture.

He had been having a very productive first season in the team before that, arguably the closest of Verstappen's team-mates since Daniel Ricciardo, though this may have been aided by the competitive re-balancing triggered by the new-for-2026 cars and power units.
Team boss Laurent Mekies says Hadjar "has been superb on and off track, especially considering this is only his second Formula 1 season, which made extending his contract an easy decision".
"The period since his injury has been a difficult one for Isack, but this extension is a testament to how much we believe in him and we can't wait to see him back out on track," Mekies added.

Hadjar has scored 71 points to Verstappen's 145 (over three more rounds) and has scored a podium in Monaco - which was taken away and then reinstated in a drawn-out appeals process over Pierre Gasly's penalty.
Attention now turns to Red Bull's second team Racing Bulls, where rookie Arvid Lindblad is virtually certain to remain but there's more intrigue surrounding team-mate Liam Lawson.

Red Bull has Formula 2 title contender Nikola Tsolov waiting in the wings for an F1 debut, but Lawson has acquitted himself very well standing in for Hadjar and has had a strong season at Racing Bulls so appears to be the favourite to stay on.

detailEn: Red Bull retains Isack Hadjar alongside Max Verstappen for F1 2027
Isack Hadjar has earned a second Red Bull Formula 1 campaign alongside four-time world champion Max Verstappen
Red Bull has confirmed it will field an unchanged Formula 1 driver line-up in 2027, with Isack Hadjar staying put alongside Max Verstappen.
Hadjar stepped up in 2026 after a rookie season at sister team Racing Bulls, and has impressed with his speed in what has historically been a difficult second Red Bull seat.

The Frenchman, who is making his return in Azerbaijan this weekend after missing three races through injury, will stay on board for another campaign in 2027 alongside Verstappen, who recently signed a contract extension to 2030.

"We’re very excited to continue our journey with Isack," said Red Bull team boss Laurent Mekies. "Since joining us at the start of the year, he has been superb on and off track, especially considering this is only his second Formula 1 season, which made extending his contract an easy decision.

"From the very beginning, Isack immersed himself in the team, spending every minute at the factory with his engineers to develop the car, always eager to learn and improve. You could see from that first weekend in Melbourne that he handled the step up with remarkable composure and had earned his place in this seat."

Despite sitting out Zandvoort, Monza and Madrid, Hadjar still holds eighth in the standings, boosted by a first Red Bull podium in Monaco to complement his maiden podium in 2025, as well as a streak of seven consecutive top-six finishes in what has largely been F1's third or fourth quickest car.

"I am really excited to continue with Oracle Red Bull Racing," the 21-year-old said. "There are so many talented people at the factory, and you’re aware of the privilege of driving for such an incredible team alongside a four-time world champion like Max.

"From the moment I signed, I set out to dedicate myself to the team, and with the support of Laurent and everyone in Milton Keynes, I’ve been able to justify the faith they’ve had in me. I’m constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day, which only makes me more excited about what lies ahead."

Racing Bulls is yet to confirm its own driver line-up for 2027, with incumbents Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad having both impressed this season while the squad also has junior driver Nikola Tsolov waiting in the wings.

items.titleZh: 威廉姆斯巴库升级：为时已晚？
items.summaryZh: 威廉姆斯为阿塞拜疆大奖赛带来以减重为主、兼有空气动力学改动的大型升级包，但车队本赛季表现远低于预期，目前仅列第九。The 比赛播客嘉宾认为，这次升级只能让车队回到本应更早达到的位置，难以改变竞争格局。

media.altZh: 威廉姆斯巴库升级：为时已晚？

items.originalTitle: 威廉姆斯巴库升级：为时已晚？
items.summaryEn: Williams is bringing a major upgrade package to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix focused largely on weight reduction with some aerodynamic changes, but the team has fallen far below expectations this season and sits ninth in the standings. Guests on The Race F1 Podcast argued the upgrade will only bring the team back to where it should have been much earlier and is unlikely to change its competitive position.
detailZh: 威廉姆斯长期以来一直宣称其重建计划的主要焦点是为抓住F1 2026年重大规则变化做好准备，但在它曾承诺要向前跃进的这个赛季，它却倒退了。
去年车队获得车队积分榜第五并登上领奖台，如今却仅以11分位列积分榜第九（比2025年同期14轮后少59分），今年平均只是第九快的赛车，单圈速度平均落后2.8%。
本周末它为阿塞拜疆大奖赛带来一套重大升级包，主要聚焦于减重，同时也包含空气动力学改动。
Edd Straw、Ben Anderson和Samarth Kanal在最新一期The 比赛 F1播客中讨论了威廉姆斯在巴库的这个重要周末。
Ben Anderson：我们知道，多携带重量就像白白送掉圈速，对吧？所以他们应该会有所进步，但我不认为这会是彻底改变命运的一步——除非他们减掉了40公斤或50公斤这种离谱的数字。我不认为这会完全改变他们的世界。我倒愿意认为他们或许能回到那个区间，即在某个周末与哈斯中最好的那辆车较量，与那两辆车中试图留在Q2底部的那一辆竞争。
我认为威廉姆斯实际上是第十好的车，拥有梅赛德斯动力单元这件事美化了它，也真正暴露了他们作为一支车队的问题。所以他们迫切需要在底盘方面看到重大进步。
Edd Straw：归根结底，他们为巴库所做的很多事情，我会称之为标准的日常事务，因为你想要达到、甚至低于重量限制。据说这会让它们低于重量限制。这样就能留出一点压舱物，这很有用，可以确保压舱物处于允许的窗口内、放在你想要的位置。
但归根结底，虽然那能带来大量性能，那实际上只是让他们回到本赛季早得多就该处于的位置。所以无论他们今年做什么，他们实际上仍在追赶，只是在消除一些负面因素。
这真的只是一步，不是吗？你只需要看到性能提升。无论如何想象，它都不会突然变成前六名的车，甚至不会变成Q3的车。
Samarth Kanal：他们现在落后太多了，这一切都是在追赶。中游对手车队已经完全在研发上超越了他们，让他们原地踏步。现在威廉姆斯落后太多，我认为这次升级只能让他们处于那个中游集团的底部。
赛车平衡存在如此根本性的问题，整个空气动力学图谱可能都需要重做。那将需要一次极其剧烈的更新——那更多是2027年而非2026年的事。
BA：实际上，自从阿斯顿·马丁把他们B版赛车带到匈牙利、并让威廉姆斯和哈斯都为那里的进步感到惊叹之后，他们就一直在给预期降温。
我认为在阿斯顿·马丁做出那样的举动之前，威廉姆斯对巴库的预期还比较乐观。现在则做了很多预期管理。我认为这是合理的，因为与今年对威廉姆斯的期望相比，他们的表现几乎可以说是令人难堪。
这非常像是2023年到2024年那个循环的重演。而这正是我真正担心威廉姆斯的地方。就像我们以前已经经历过这一幕。
他们在2025年从中走出来得非常好，但2025年的一切都是关于‘我们很早就用风洞测试2026年赛车，我们现在的基准是成为中游集团之首，然后寻求缩小差距’。而他们刚刚远远偏离了那条轨道。
‘一切都在燃烧’——威廉姆斯F1 2026灾难被彻底揭露
别指望威廉姆斯的升级能让它具备竞争力
ES：车队领队James Vowles在赛季初表示，他们新的基准是去年获得的第五名。所以按照他们自己的标准，他们没有达到，原因各种各样。赛车交付晚了。显然它超重，下压力不足，高斜率概念没有奏效，还有操控麻烦，这种多年来持续存在的三轮行驶问题，他们仍在与之斗争。
ES：要评判他们，我们需要看看他们明年年初会做什么。对我来说那才是关键，因为他们必须消除交付延迟的问题。他们必须达到重量要求。他们必须有正确的空气动力学套件，并且至少在中游集团中表现不错。
因为如果他们做不到，那才是真正该敲响警钟的时候。
detailEn: After declaring for so long that the main focus of its rebuilding programme was being ready to capitalise on Formula 1's major 2026 regulation changes, Williams has tumbled backwards in the season when it had promised to leap forwards.

Fifth in the constructors' championship and a podium finisher last year, now it's ninth in the standings on only 11 points (59 fewer than at this stage, after 14 rounds, in 2025), and has been only the ninth-fastest car on average this year, an average of 2.8% down on single-lap pace.
This weekend it's bringing a major upgrade package to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, focused largely on weight reduction but also featuring aerodynamic changes.
Edd Straw, Ben Anderson and Samarth Kanal debated Williams's big Baku weekend on the latest episode of The Race F1 Podcast.

Ben Anderson: We know that carrying excess weight is like giving away free laptime, isn't it? So they should make a step but I don't think it will make an absolutely life-changing one - unless they're taking out something like 40kg or 50kg, some nonsensical amount. I don't think it's going to completely change their world. I'd like to think they might get back into that zone of kind of fighting with whichever is the best of the Haases on a given weekend, whichever one of those cars is trying to be at the bottom of Q2.

I think the Williams is actually the 10th-best car and the fact it's got the Mercedes power unit flatters it and really exposes them as a team. So they desperately need to see a big step on the chassis side.

Edd Straw: Ultimately, a lot of what they're doing for Baku is what I'd sort of call the standard housekeeping stuff because you want to be on or in fact under the weight limit. And apparently this will put them under the weight limit. So that'll allow them a little bit of ballast, which is useful to have for making sure you've got the ballast within the allowed window where you want it to be.

But ultimately, while that's a load of performance, that's really only getting them back to where they should have been much earlier in the season. So whatever they do this year, they're still really playing catch-up and just eliminating some of the negatives.
It's just one step really, isn't it? You just need to see the performance improvement. It's not going to suddenly turn into a top-six car by any stretch of the imagination or even a Q3 car.

Samarth Kanal: They are so far behind now that this is all catching up. Rival midfield teams have completely outdeveloped them, left them standing still. and now Williams is so far behind that I think this upgrade can only put them at the bottom of that midfield set.
There's such a fundamental issue in car balance, the whole aero map needs to probably be redone. That's going to need an incredibly drastic update - that's more for 2027 than 2026.
BA: They've been talking it down actually since Aston Martin bought their B-spec car to Hungary and kind of wowed certainly Williams and Haas with the step they took there.

I think before Aston Martin did what they did, Williams were a bit more bullish about what they were expecting from Baku. Now there's been a lot of expectation management. I think that's a reasonable thing to do because compared to expectations of Williams this year, they've been pretty much embarrassing.
This is very much the 2023 into 2024 cycle repeating. And that's the thing I really worry about with Williams. It's like we've been here before.

They came out of it really well in 2025, but then 2025 was all about 'we're in the windtunnel with the 2026 car really early, our baseline now is to be top of the midfield and then look to bridge the gap'. And they've just fallen way off that track.
'Everything was on fire' - Williams's F1 2026 disaster laid bare
Don't expect Williams's upgrade to make it competitive

ES: James Vowles, the team principal, said at the start of the season that their new baseline is the fifth place they got last year. So they've fallen short by their own standards and there's all sorts of reasons for that. The car was late. Obviously it's overweight, downforce isn't there and the high rake concept didn't work, there are handling troubles, this sort of three-wheeling problem that's been persistent over a number of years that they're still battling.

ES: To judge them, we need to see what they do at the start of next year. That for me is the critical thing because they've got to eliminate the problems with being late. They've got to be on the weight. They've got to have the right aero package and be performing decently in that midfield at the very least.
Because if they're not there, then that's when you really start to sound the alarm bells.
keyPointsZh: 威廉姆斯目前以11分位列车队积分榜第九，比2025年同期少59分，今年平均单圈速度落后2.8%，仅列第九快。
车队领队James Vowles赛季初表示新车队基准是去年的第五名，但赛车交付延迟、超重、下压力不足、高斜率概念未奏效，且长期存在三轮行驶等操控问题。
嘉宾认为对手中游车队已完全超越威廉姆斯，彻底解决赛车平衡与空气动力学图谱问题需要更大幅度的更新，更可能指向2027年而非2026年。
keyPointsEn: Williams sits ninth in the constructors' championship on only 11 points, 59 fewer than at the same stage in 2025, and has been only the ninth-fastest car on average this year, 2.8% down on single-lap pace.

items.summaryZh: F1将前往巴库开启三连赛的首站，这条赛道对空气动力学效率要求极高，各车队在技术层面有六个值得关注的方面。

media.altZh: 阿塞拜疆大奖赛六大F1技术看点

items.originalTitle: 阿塞拜疆大奖赛六大F1技术看点
items.summaryEn: Formula 1 heads to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the first race of a punishing triple-header that could prove defining for the world championship, with six technical storylines worth watching.
detailZh: 一级方程式即将来到阿塞拜疆大奖赛，这是艰苦三连赛的第一站，而这三场比赛可能会对世界冠军的归属起到决定性作用。
但这并不是车队推出重大升级的理想之地，通常在这样一连串背靠背比赛中他们都会这么做。
巴库赛道的布局拥有长长的直道，这使得空气动力学效率比下压力更为重要，因此重点更多放在优化而不是改进上。
这就是为什么梅赛德斯和法拉利等车队预计会再等一等，才去冲刺他们很可能是一年中最后一套的研发升级包。
但本周末仍有许多值得关注的技战术看点。
在F1新规则时代开局不顺之后，威廉姆斯车队希望阿塞拜疆大奖赛能成为其复苏的起点。
此前一直按兵不动、未对赛车进行大改，如今所有人的目光都集中在其全新的更轻底盘上，车队希望这能成为摆脱车手们迄今被迫背负的多余重量的关键一步。
这次威廉姆斯升级特别引人关注之处在于，车队领队詹姆斯·沃利斯谈到新底盘在制造方式上蕴含创新。
“这次学到的经验将为我们未来五年打下基础，”他最近告诉The 比赛。
“围场里没有任何其他底盘是像我们这样造出来的。我可以向你保证这一点。”
威廉姆斯究竟做了什么还没有被详细解释，但据了解，这围绕一些制造工艺展开，这些工艺让车队减掉了超出正常预期的更多重量。
但需要提醒一句。沃勒斯和车手们都没有期待性能会出现改变格局的飞跃。
正如亚历克斯·阿尔本所说："这会是一个不错的进步，但是否会是全面的进步呢？我对此抱有希望，但我不认为会是。"
阿斯顿·马丁几乎把所有空气动力学升级都留到了匈牙利大奖赛期间的中季底盘大改款上，车队领队兼技术管理合伙人阿德里安·纽维削减了重量，并解决了他最初的 AMR26 概念车的种种弱点。
由于车队希望确保以良好状态开启2027赛季，它不想把研发延续到本赛季末，这就是它放缓升级频率的原因。
但这并不意味着它不会带来新部件——在巴库，它预计将引入一些更轻量化的部件，以便更接近768公斤的重量限制。
车队的赛道事务主管迈克·克拉克在西班牙大奖赛上表示，这些改动很可能不会引起注意，因为车队只需向国际汽联正式申报那些外观不同的部件。
“我们接下来还会带来一些新部件，有些必须申报，有些则不用，”他说，“我不认为（阿斯顿·马丁的研发）已经彻底完成，但我认为我们不会再有像布达佩斯那样的升级了。”
虽然厂队法拉利以及它的客户车队之一哈斯从9月初的蒙扎意大利大奖赛起就已经使用了马拉内罗最新的ADUO 2规格引擎，但凯迪拉克到目前为止一直没有动手。
由于安装经过修改的动力单元存在复杂性，需要更换新的部件，凯迪拉克希望在蒙扎和马德里赛道的连续双站比赛结束后，再决定是否启用它。
车队目前已放行，允许塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯在巴库使用它，而瓦尔特里·博塔斯则还得再等一段时间。
发动机升级带来的额外动力对凯迪拉克来说将是一次广受欢迎的提升，车队同时还会引入一些小幅空气动力学升级。
ADUO 2（第二阶段升级单元）很可能也将成为法拉利关注的话题，因为厂商正在权衡本赛季余下比赛的动力单元计划。
夏尔·勒克莱尔在意大利大奖赛发生撞车时正在使用的ADUO 2发动机，很可能将在阿塞拜疆重返赛道进行评估，但他也有可能拿到一台全新的发动机，以支撑他跑完本赛季的剩余征程。
巴库的长直道意味着这里是接受更换引擎而退后发车位置的好地方。
迈凯伦的H翼连同另一项升级一同回归。
迈凯伦自夏休期以来从其MCL40上挖掘出了丰富的性能提升空间，在快速和中速弯角上取得了重大进步。
不过车队仍然清楚一些核心弱点，尤其是在直线性能和低速弯道方面。
对于拥有那条非常长的发车/终点大直道的巴库站，迈凯伦将重新启用其低阻力的“H翼”尾翼，该部件在意大利大奖赛上首次投入使用。
车队还计划评估另一套升级套件，希望能在此前相比主要对手损失圈速的领域带来提升。
技术总监罗布·马歇尔表示，规则保持稳定意味着没有理由停止继续推出升级。
“由于规则将延续到下个赛季，且前方竞争如此接近，我们持续研发赛车的动力依然很高，”他说。
巴库的赛道布局对当前能源匮乏的赛车来说是有利有弊。
由1号弯到16号弯组成的低速急弯和城市赛段，应当能提供大量为电池充电并释放额外电能的机会。
但从16号弯一直延伸到第一个弯角的极长直道，将是电池效率和电量状态至关重要的地方。
各车队需要评估的一点是，2026年赛车下压力的降低是否意味着18/19号弯的高速组合弯仍然可以全油门通过。
如果可以的话，那将意味着一种与需要升挡不同的能量部署模式，这会为能量回收带来一定的提升。
另一个可能在整个周末带来麻烦的问题是，在练习赛和排位赛中，暖胎圈慢速行驶的赛车与做出冲刺圈快圈赛车之间可能出现的巨大速度差。
各车队会希望对他们的电机发电一体机进行编程，在排位赛中尽可能晚地、直到计时线之前才消耗电池电量，这意味着在此之前沿主直道行驶时内燃机的输出会较慢。
这意味着这些赛车的速度曲线将与那些从16号弯驶出时就已最大化利用能量的赛车截然不同，因此后者将以快得多的速度接近起点/终点线。
detailEn: Formula 1 heads to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix for the first race of a punishing triple-header that could prove defining for the world championship.
But it is not an ideal place for teams to unleash the kind of major upgrades they typically would for such a run of back-to-backs.
The layout of the Baku circuit with its long straights puts a premium on aero efficiency over downforce, so the focus is more on optimisation rather than improvement.
That is why teams such as Mercedes and Ferrari are expected to wait a little bit longer before gunning for what will likely be their final development packages of the year.
But there remains plenty of tech intrigue to keep an eye out for this weekend.
After a troubled start to F1's new rules era, Williams hopes that the Azerbaijan GP will mark the start of its recovery.

Having held fire on a major car revamp until now, all eyes will be on the new, lighter chassis that it hopes will mark a step-change in getting rid of the excess weight its drivers have been forced to carry around so far.

What will make the Williams upgrade especially interesting is that team principal James Vowles has talked of there being innovation at the heart of the new chassis when it comes to how it has been manufactured.
"This learning will be one that kicks us off for the next five years," he told The Race recently.
"There's no other chassis in the grid made the way we've done it. I can give you an assurance of that."

Exactly what Williams has done has not been explained in detail yet, but it is understood to revolve around some manufacturing processes that have allowed the team to shed off more mass than would normally be expected.
But a word of caution. Neither Vowles nor the drivers are anticipating a game-changing leap in performance.
As Alex Albon said: "It's going to be a good step, but is it going to be the full step? I'm hopeful for it, but I don't think it would be."

Aston Martin saved pretty much all its aero upgrades for its mid-season chassis overhaul at the Hungarian GP, as team principal and managing technical partner Adrian Newey slashed weight and addressed the weaknesses of his first AMR26 concept.
With the team wanting to make sure it starts 2027 on the front foot, it does not want to continue development into the end of this season, which is why it has wound down its update rate.
But that does not mean it will not bring new parts - and in Baku it is set to introduce some lighter components to get down closer to the 768kg weight limit.
Chief trackside officer Mike Krack said at the Spanish GP that the changes will likely go under the radar, as teams only have to officially declare to the FIA components that look different.

"We still bring some more parts going forward, some will be declared because we have to, some will not," he said. "I don't think it [Aston Martin's development] is completely finished, but I don't think that we will have an upgrade like Budapest."
While the works Ferrari team and one of its customers, Haas, have both used Maranello's latest ADUO 2-spec engine since the Italian GP at Monza in early September, Cadillac has held fire so far.
Due to complications of installing the revised power unit, which requires new parts, Cadillac wanted to wait until after the Monza/Madrid double-header before committing to it.
It has now given the green light for Sergio Perez to run it in Baku, while Valtteri Bottas will have to wait a little bit longer.
The extra power on offer from the engine upgrade will be a welcome boost to Cadillac, which will also be introducing some small aerodynamic upgrades as well.
ADUO 2 will likely be a topic of interest at Ferrari as well, as the manufacturer weighs up its power unit plans over the remainder of the season.

Charles Leclerc's ADUO 2 engine, which was in use when he crashed in the Italian GP, is likely to return to the track for evaluation in Azerbaijan, but it is also possible that he may get a totally fresh one as well to see him through to the end of the campaign.
Baku's long straights mean that it is a good place to take a grid drop for an engine swap.
McLaren's H-wing returns alongside another update
McLaren has unlocked a rich seam of performance from its MCL40 since the summer break, having made big gains in fast- and medium-speed corners.
The team is still mindful of some core weaknesses, though, especially when it comes to straightline performance and low-speed turns.
For Baku, which features that very long start/finish straight, McLaren will bring back into action its low-drag 'H-wing' that it raced for the first time at the Italian GP.
It is also set to evaluate another upgrade package that it hopes can deliver gains in areas where it is giving away laptime to its main rivals.
Chief technical officer Rob Marshall said that rules stability meant there was little reason not to keep the upgrades coming.
"With regulatory continuity into next season and the competition at the front so close, our motivation to keep developing the car remains high," he said.
The Baku layout is a mixed blessing for the current energy-starved cars.
The tight, low-speed corners and city section that make up the sequence from Turn 1 through to Turn 16 should offer plenty of opportunity to charge the battery and unleash added electrical power.
But the extremely long run from Turn 16 all the way through to the first corner is one where battery efficiency and state of charge are going to be critical.
One thing that teams will need to evaluate is whether the reduced downforce of the 2026 cars means that the fast Turn 18/19 sequence can still be taken flat.
If it can, then that will mean a different deployment pattern compared to if it requires a lift, which will deliver a bit of a boost for energy harvesting.
One other issue, which could cause some trouble over the weekend, is of potential big speed differentials between cars on outlaps and cars on push laps in practice and qualifying.

Teams will want to programme their MGU-Ks to not burn up any battery until as late as possible before the timing line in qualifying, which will mean running slower on the internal combustion engine beforehand down the main straight.
That means a speed profile very different from cars that will have maximised energy usage coming out of Turn 16, and that will be approaching the start/finish line much quicker as a result.

items.titleZh: 逃离F1泡沫后我学到了什么
items.summaryZh: The 比赛的Scott Mitchell-Malm在休陪产假离开F1三个月后，分享了他以车迷视角观看比赛的新认识，包括对冲刺赛周末的意外好感以及对2026规则和F1官方宣传的批评。
items.originalTitle: 逃离F1泡沫后我学到了什么
items.summaryEn: The Race's Scott Mitchell-Malm shares what he learned after stepping away from F1 for three months on paternity leave, including a newfound appreciation for sprint weekends and criticism of the 2026 rules and F1's messaging.
detailZh: 在泡沫中待了近十年是很长的时间。其他人待得更久，但连续第九个赛季奔波或工作近200场比赛，意味着F1占据了我生活的很大一部分。
无论好坏，在围场内关注F1与从远处观看是不同的。这既是一种巨大的特权，也是一种相当大的负担，取决于具体情况——而且，为了完成工作所需的信息，我越来越依赖一种精心策划的研究F1的方法，这也让我看待F1的视角变得非常狭窄。
我已经很久没有为了享受而观看一场F1比赛了，也没有在一个周末不仔细阅读数千字的引述、数小时的数据或车载镜头的情况下关注比赛。尽管F1媒体经常与车迷交流，有时还代表车迷发声，但我们很少拥有相同的视角。同样，无论好坏。
今年夏天不同。我休了三个月的陪产假，专注于我三岁的儿子和去年九月出生的女儿，从而逃离了那个长期支配我大部分时间的泡沫。
在此期间举行了七场比赛，我最初的一个想法是：如果我不必关心F1，我还会关心多少？尤其是在这个由于新规则而在职业和个人层面多次考验我耐心的赛季中。
我注意到的第一件事是，我竟然没有注意到它的发生。
在赛车甚至还没上赛道的前一天，F1的马戏团就已经全面展开。媒体日在围场里是件大事，我知道有些车迷非常清楚这件事，并且知道要留意引述甚至关注车手新闻发布会。
这是一个庞大的运作，以喂养一个比以往更大、更饥渴的内容机器。所有车手都要与各种广播公司和文字媒体交谈，还有几位车队人员也会发言，车队也在制作自己的内容。规模令人难以置信地庞大。
我理解人们对这些内容有兴趣，我并不是在贬低它。但我常常觉得这有点浪费。
预览内容被采用后的保质期很短，而且在双赛和三赛（如今如此常见）中，我们通常几天前就已经听过这些人的发言了。F1几年前确实试图取消这一天，我认为原则是正确的，即使试验的方式没有成功。
我常常想——鉴于我们自己的分析显示周四的关注度并没有显著上升——这在多大程度上是一种自我服务的行为，已经膨胀成F1足迹的很大一部分，却没有实际价值来证明其合理性。而且我很惊讶，一旦我不在场，周四就这样完全被我忽略了。
至少有几次，我只是看到周五有练习赛，才想起‘这个周末是X比赛’。我知道这很大程度上受我自身情况的影响，但这正是重点：对我来说，最大的转变是从一个占据大量时间和精力的日子，变成一个甚至不会注意到的日子。
我想知道这对多少车迷来说也是如此。
我从车迷角度观看的两个比赛周末是冲刺赛。它们的功能实际上比我预想的要稍微奇怪一些。
在正常周末，要真正投入三场练习赛是很困难的（而且周五根本无法实时关注）。正如我所说，我甚至没有注意到其中一些练习赛的开始！
这意味着我在观看排位赛时，与可能的情况相比，存在很大的知识缺口——我有时确实感觉到了这一点。这也不可避免地延续到正赛中，而且不是好事。这不是‘哦，我不知道会发生什么’，而是‘哦，事情正在发生，但我并不真正理解’。
但我发现冲刺赛周末出人意料地适合快速了解情况，而且不会让我对周末的理解被拖累。无论是周五晚上错过了白天的活动，只是快速了解一下冲刺排位赛，还是在周六某个时候找时间看冲刺赛，它们都是更轻松、更好的休闲观赛体验。
所以，冲刺赛实际上比我预想的要享受得多——尽管比赛本身还是那样。
我一直接受F1的主要论点，即冲刺赛周末能带来两场更好的同类观看赛事。冲刺排位赛比FP2好，冲刺赛比FP3好。但这并不改变我认为比赛通常不好的事实，我希望F1在冲刺赛制整体上做更多——在家观看冲刺赛也强烈地强化了这一点。
这已经是旧闻了，因为在我写这篇文章时，这些评论是很久以前发表的，但从远处看，F1和Stefano Domenicali关于车迷想要什么的言论令人恼火。尤其是这并不是今年第一次发生这种情况。
我们现在都熟悉Domenicali觉得有必要相当好斗地面对任何对F1产品的挑战。即使面对令人不安的现实：2026年的规则是一个极其糟糕的妥协，经过广泛审议后，明年将有许多变化来解决那些据说并不存在的问题。
我愿意认为这只是表达方式不对，而且比预期的更糟，但我能理解为什么这么多车迷觉得这种宣传近乎对‘传统’车迷的蔑视，因为所谓的指标以及George Lucas显然非常重要的证词——实际上，新车迷喜欢这个版本的F1，他们不关心技术信息或车手驾驶技术的细微差别。
我个人认为，这是对那些确实重视大奖赛这些精彩元素的车迷的错误轻视——而且我认为这低估了新车迷，因为我们遇到过很多通过《Drive to Survive》进入F1的人，他们很快就想要更深入的报道。
这与我看到的另一件事混在一起，很糟糕，那件事体现了现代F1某些方面充斥的夸张：夏季休赛期期间预告的某个东西，结果只是没有任何深度或实质的宣传材料。
这在职业层面会让我恼火，但作为车迷随意看到时，我觉得这至少是判断失误：我认为今年不是炒作一个达不到期望的东西的时候。
关于2026年规则，我愿意坚持的一个观点是，比赛中确实有一些好的元素。它们只是被有问题的极端情况所掩盖。
最初，我从赛道边观看新车如何移动的特权位置支持我的立场（即使这仍然让包括维斯塔潘在内的车手不满），现在我从远处看到了这套规则的最好和最坏之处。
蒙扎比我想象的要好得多，而且赛车仍然可以在各种赛道上紧密跟随，尽管真正的超车可能很难——如果我再也看不到2026年马德里赛道比赛的一圈，我会很高兴。
有几次让我失望的是，很难跟踪谁做得好谁做得不好。当你在周末工作并身处其中时，信息会源源不断地传来，几乎只要在那里就能形成一幅图景——所以当比赛中发生事情时，通常会有一些背景或理解来帮助理解。
但我看到了太多感觉像是第一圈随机的电池使用情况，以及赛车上升或后退，却不真正确定这些人做得好还是不好。这取决于算法吗？车手在关键时刻是否比以往任何时候都更加被动？
我发现有时几乎难以看到这项运动的本质，这真的令人沮丧。所以在赞德沃特，Verstappen谈到F1在这方面太容易时，我深有共鸣。
尽管如此，我对2027年将发生的变化感到好奇和乐观。我在开头写道，我很好奇当F1变得更休闲时，我与它的关系会是什么——我想知道我是否仍然关心。我想我最大的收获是我仍然关心。
我有点担心我不再喜欢它，或者当我不再被迫关注时，我的兴趣会消退。这从来不是我的首要任务——这正是休假的意义所在！——我承认有几次因为无聊而没看一两场比赛。
但对F1的热情仍然非常强烈。而且现在也许基于一种稍微不同的视角，而不仅仅是我长期以来从特权位置获得的视角。
detailEn: Nearly a decade in a bubble is a long time. Others have done plenty longer but a ninth consecutive season travelling to or working nearly 200 races means Formula 1 has dominated a huge part of my life.

For better and worse, following F1 inside the paddock is not the same as watching from afar. It is both an immense privilege and quite a burden, depending on circumstance - and an increasingly curated method of studying F1 for the information I have needed to do my job gave me a very narrow lens to view it through, too.

It has been a long time since I watched an F1 race to enjoy it, or followed a weekend without poring over thousands of words of quotes and hours of data or onboard footage. Though the F1 media talks to, and sometimes on behalf of, fans an awful lot, we rarely have the same perspective. Again, for better and worse.

This summer was different. I stepped away for three months on paternity leave to focus on my three-year-old son and my daughter, who was born last September, and in doing so escaped the bubble that had dictated so much of my time for so long.

With seven races taking place in this period, a very early thought I had was: how much will I still care about F1 if I don't have to? Especially in the middle of a season that, thanks to the new rules, has tested my patience professionally and personally more than once.
One of the very first things I noticed was something I didn't notice happening.

The day before cars even hit the track, F1's circus is already in full swing. Media day is such a big deal in the paddock, and I know there are fans who are very aware it's a thing and do know to look out for quotes or even follow driver press conferences.

It is a colossal operation to feed a content machine that is bigger and hungrier than it's ever been. All the drivers speak to various broadcasters and the written media, there's a couple of team people that speak too, teams are doing their own content production. It's incredibly vast.
I get that there is interest in it, and I'm not knocking that. But I have often thought it feels like a bit of a waste.

There's very little shelf life for what preview content is picked up and often in double-headers and triple-headers (which are so common these days) we have typically heard from all these people a few days ago. F1 did try to phase this day out a few years ago, and I think the principle was right even if the way it was trialled didn't work.

I've often wondered - given we can see in our own analytics that there isn't any major uptick in attention on a Thursday - how much this is a self-serving exercise that has ballooned into a massive part of F1's footprint without actually having the value to merit it. And I was surprised how early on it was that the Thursdays just completely passed me by once I was not there.

There were at least a couple of occasions where it was only seeing that there had been a practice session on Friday that I remembered 'it's race X this weekend'. I know that's heavily influenced by my own circumstances, but that is the point: it was the single-biggest shift for me from a day that took up a huge amount of time and energy to one that did not even register.
And I wonder how many fans that goes for.
Two of the race weekends I watched from the fan position were sprint events. These actually have a slightly stranger function than I thought they would.

On normal weekends it was difficult to really engage fully with three practice sessions to labour through (and Friday just not being possible to follow in the moment). As I said, I didn't even notice some of them starting!

That meant I'd watch qualifying with quite a big knowledge deficit compared to what was possible - and I felt that sometimes. It also inevitably carries over into the race, and not in a good way. It's not, 'Ooh, I don't know what's going to happen' it's, 'Oh, things are happening and I'm not really comprehending it'.

But I found the sprint weekends surprisingly good for quick-fire catch-ups of what's going on, without really feeling like I had my comprehension of the weekend dragged down. They were an easier and better experience to follow casually, whether that was a Friday evening where the daytime action has been missed and it's simply to have a quick catch-up with sprint qualifying, or finding the time to watch the sprint at some point on the Saturday.
So the sprints, actually, I enjoyed a lot more than I thought - even though the races are what they are.

I've long been accepting of F1's primary argument that the sprint weekend makes for two better like-for-like viewing events. Sprint qualifying is better than an FP2, the sprint race is better than FP3. That doesn't change the fact I think the races usually aren't good, and I would like F1 to do more with the sprint format overall - this was also emphatically reinforced by sitting through the sprints at home.

This is old news now, because the comments were made a while ago as I write this, but the messaging from F1 and Stefano Domenicali when it comes to what fans supposedly want was a grating experience from a distance. Especially as it wasn't the first time that's happened this year.

We are all familiar now with Domenicali feeling the need to confront any challenge to F1's product quite combatively. Even against the uncomfortable reality that the 2026 rules have been an extremely bad compromise and many changes are coming next year, after extensive deliberation, to address the issues that supposedly don't exist.

I'd like to think it just comes out the wrong way, and worse than intended, but I can see why so many fans feel like the propaganda flirts with borderline contempt for 'traditional' fans because of supposed metrics and the apparently very important testimony from George Lucas that, actually, new fans love this version of F1 and they don't care about technical information or the nuance of a driver's racecraft.

Personally, I believe that's wrongly dismissive of fans who do value such wonderful elements of grand prix racing - and I think it sells newer fans short, because we have come across plenty who got into F1 watching Drive to Survive, for example, and swiftly wanted deeper coverage.

It blended poorly with another thing I saw that exemplified the hyperbole that engulfs some aspects of modern F1: the teaser of something dropping during the summer break, which just turned out to be promotional material that had no depth or substance whatsoever.

That would annoy me in a professional capacity but seeing it casually as a fan it felt ill-judged at best: I don't think this is the year to be hyping up something that doesn't live up to expectations.
A hill I am happy to die on with the 2026 rules is there are elements of the racing that are actually good. They're just clouded by problematic extremities.

Having initially championed my position from the luxury of watching trackside and seeing how the new cars moved around (even if that was still to the displeasure of drivers including Max Verstappen) I have now seen the best and worst of this ruleset from afar.

Monza was a great deal better than I feared, and it remains the case that cars can follow closely on a range of tracks even though proper overtaking can be hard to come by - if I never see a lap of the 2026 Madring race again, I'll be a happy man.

What disappointed me a few times was just how hard it was to follow who's doing well and who isn't. When you're working the weekend and in the middle of it all, there is a drip feed of information and a picture starts to form almost just by being there - so then when things happen in the race, there's usually some morsel of context or understanding that helps put it into context.

But I saw so much of what felt like first-lap randomness with battery usage, and cars rising up or falling back, without really being sure if these people were doing a good job or a bad job. Is it algorithm-dependent? Are the drivers more passive participants in crucial moments than ever before?
I found it really frustrating to almost struggle to see the sport in this sometimes. So it really resonated at Zandvoort, where Verstappen talked about F1 being too easy in that regard.

Still, I am curious and optimistic about what will change in 2027. I was not being glib when I wrote at the top that I was curious to discover what my relationship would be with F1 when it was more casual - I wanted to know if I still cared. And I think the biggest takeaway for me is I still do.

I was a bit worried that I wouldn't like it anymore, or my interest would fade when I wasn't obliged. It was never the number-one priority for me - that was the whole point of taking time away! - and I admitted I tuned out of one or two races out of boredom a couple of times.
But the enthusiasm for F1 is still very much there. And it is perhaps now underpinned by a slightly different perspective beyond just the one gleaned from the privileged position I had for so long.

items.titleZh: F1正赛为何是305公里？1950至2027年赛程距离演变
items.summaryZh: F1正赛距离由超过305公里所需的最少圈数决定，摩纳哥以260公里为例外；从1950年无统一标准到1989年确立305公里规则，2027年标准将降至290公里。

items.originalTitle: 为什么F1正赛长度为305公里？从1950年到2027年的比赛距离
items.summaryEn: Formula 1 race distances are determined by the minimum number of laps required to exceed 305 kilometres, with Monaco as the only exception at 260 kilometres. From no standardised distance in 1950 to the 305-kilometre rule set in 1989, the standard is set to drop to 290 kilometres in 2027.
detailZh: 为什么F1正赛长度为305公里？从1950年到2027年的比赛距离
305公里、两小时，或包含中断在内的三小时：F1比赛距离受明确规则约束。我们解释这些规则自1950年以来如何演变、为什么摩纳哥是例外，以及为什么2027年比赛将变短。
一场F1大奖赛的赛程超过305公里。更准确地说，一场比赛由超过305公里所需的最少圈数构成。唯一的例外是摩纳哥，其最低距离为260公里。
实际比赛时间还有两小时限制。如果比赛中断，包含中断时间在内的总时长不得超过三小时。这是现行F1规则的规定。
但情况并非一直如此标准化。在世界锦标赛的最初几十年里，一些比赛的赛程几乎是现在的两倍。而到2027年，距离将再次缩短。比赛实际持续多久以及完成多少圈，也在我们的文章《一场F1比赛持续多久？》中有所说明。
1950年代：比赛长达500公里
1950年F1世界锦标赛开始时，并没有标准的比赛距离。组织者在很大程度上可以自由决定自己赛事的长度，导致差异相当大。
在银石举行的史上第一场世界锦标赛比赛跑了70圈、325公里。冠军尼诺·法里纳用时2小时13分钟完成。相比之下，在蒙扎的赛季收官战中，法里纳跑了80圈、约504公里。他驾驶了将近三个小时。
更长的是印第安纳波利斯500，从1950年到1960年计入世界锦标赛。它共200圈、805公里，至今仍是世界锦标赛历史上圈数和距离都最多的比赛。
1958年，管理机构引入了更严格的限制。比赛距离被设定在300至500公里之间，最长时限为两小时。
在随后的几年里，大多数大奖赛的赛程在300至400公里之间。上限最终定为400公里。
1971年：最长约322公里
1971赛季，最大比赛距离从400公里降至约322公里。比赛因此明显变短。
同一赛季有一个极端例子。在纽博格林北环举行的德国大奖赛仅持续了12圈。由于赛道长度近23公里，这仍是正常完成的世界锦标赛比赛中圈数最少的。
在1970年代和1980年代，大多数比赛稳定在约300至320公里。
1989年，比赛距离被标准化为最低305公里。目的是确保比赛能在两小时内完成。
此后，每场大奖赛都由使总距离刚好超过305公里所需的最少圈数构成。这一基本原则至今仍然有效。
例如在2026年，这意味着在赛道长度超过七公里的斯帕-弗朗科尔尚为44圈。巴库为51圈，雪邦为56圈。摩纳哥圈数最多，为78圈。
摩纳哥例外：为什么比赛只有260公里
摩纳哥是唯一不适用305公里规则的赛道。这个公国的比赛为78圈、约260公里。
原因是速度。这条街道赛道仅长3.337公里，而且狭窄多弯。平均速度远低于其他赛道。
因此，在摩纳哥跑超过305公里可能会因平均速度低而导致比赛异常漫长。这就是摩纳哥最低比赛距离为260公里的原因。
2011年加拿大站：迄今为止最长的F1比赛
多年来，只有对实际比赛时间的两小时限制。没有规则规定计入中断后比赛可以持续多久。2011年加拿大大奖赛后，这种情况改变了。
蒙特利尔的大雨使比赛中断了约两个小时。简森·巴顿最终在一次惊人的逆转后获胜。官方比赛用时为4:04:39.537，成为F1历史上最长的比赛。
FIA迅速作出回应。从2012年起，包含中断在内的比赛不得超过四小时。实际比赛的两小时限制仍然保留。2021赛季，总时限被缩减为三小时。
2021年比利时站：最短比赛和新积分规则
2021年在斯帕-弗朗科尔尚，F1经历了相反的极端情况。持续降雨意味着车队只在安全车后绕行。官方成绩中仅计入一圈。
根据当时有效的规则，仍然授予了半分。这引发了广泛批评。
因此，自2022年起，对于缩短的比赛，只要在无安全车或虚拟安全车的情况下完成至少两圈，积分便按滑动比例授予：
两圈至比赛距离的25%：前五名获得积分（6-4-3-2-1）。
自2023年起，当暂停的比赛恢复后，即使最终未完成全部预定距离，也授予全额积分。
部分比赛周末在大奖赛之外还设有冲刺赛。冲刺赛约100公里，约为正常比赛距离的三分之一，通常持续约半小时。
没有强制进站。前八名获得积分（8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1）。2026年赛历中有六场冲刺赛。该赛制的完整细节可在《F1冲刺赛：你需要知道的一切》中找到。
从2027年起，标准比赛距离将从305公里降至290公里。据FIA称，这相当于减少约两到三圈。
F1委员会已批准这一缩减，但仍需FIA世界汽车运动理事会最终批准。
基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯，马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，兰多·诺里斯，迈凯伦
与此同时，目前对受中断影响比赛的三小时总时限将被废除。取而代之的是，将为比赛活动的结束引入固定的硬性截止时间。实际比赛的两小时限制将保留。
detailEn: Why is a Formula 1 race 305 kilometres long? Race distances from 1950 to 2027

305 kilometres, two hours, or three hours including interruptions: Formula 1 race distances are governed by clear rules. We explain how those rules have evolved since 1950, why Monaco is an exception and why races will become shorter in 2027.

A Formula 1 Grand Prix is more than 305 kilometres long. More precisely, a race consists of the minimum number of laps required to exceed 305 kilometres. The only exception is Monaco, where the minimum distance is 260 kilometres.

There is also a two-hour limit on actual racing time. If a race is suspended, the total duration including the interruption may not exceed three hours. That is what the current Formula 1 regulations stipulate.

But it has not always been this standardised. During the first decades of the World Championship, some races were almost twice as long. And in 2027, the distance will be reduced again. How long a race lasts in practice and how many laps are completed is also explained in our article How long does a Formula 1 race last?
The 1950s: Races of up to 500 kilometres

When the Formula 1 World Championship began in 1950, there was no standard race distance. Organisers were largely free to determine the length of their own events, resulting in considerable variation.

The very first World Championship race at Silverstone ran for 70 laps and 325 kilometres. Winner Nino Farina completed it in 2 hours and 13 minutes. At the season finale in Monza, by contrast, Farina raced for 80 laps and around 504 kilometres. He was behind the wheel for almost three hours.

Longer still was the Indianapolis 500, which counted towards the World Championship from 1950 to 1960. At 200 laps and 805 kilometres, it remains the race with both the highest number of laps and the greatest distance in World Championship history.
In 1958, the governing body introduced much tighter restrictions. Race distances were set at between 300 and 500 kilometres, with a maximum duration of two hours.
In the years that followed, most Grands Prix covered between 300 and 400 kilometres. The upper limit was eventually 400 kilometres.
1971: A maximum of around 322 kilometres
For the 1971 season, the maximum race distance was reduced from 400 to around 322 kilometres. Races consequently became noticeably shorter.

One extreme example came that same season. The German Grand Prix on the Nürburgring Nordschleife lasted just 12 laps. With the circuit measuring almost 23 kilometres, it remains the lowest number of laps in a regularly completed World Championship race.
During the 1970s and 1980s, most races settled at around 300 to 320 kilometres.
In 1989, the race distance was standardised at a minimum of 305 kilometres. The aim was to ensure that a race could be completed within two hours.
Since then, each Grand Prix has consisted of the minimum number of laps required to take the total distance just beyond 305 kilometres. The basic principle remains in place today.
In 2026, for example, that means 44 laps at Spa-Francorchamps, where the circuit is more than seven kilometres long. Baku has 51 laps and Sepang 56. Monaco has the highest lap count at 78.
The Monaco exception: Why the race is only 260 kilometres
Monaco is the only circuit where the 305-kilometre rule does not apply. The race in the Principality covers 78 laps and around 260 kilometres.
The reason is speed. The street circuit is only 3.337 kilometres long, as well as being narrow and twisty. Average speeds are considerably lower than at other circuits.

Covering more than 305 kilometres in Monaco would therefore risk producing an exceptionally long race because of the low average speed. That is why Monaco has a minimum race distance of 260 kilometres.
Canada 2011: The longest Formula 1 race to date

For many years, there was only a two-hour limit on actual racing time. There was no rule governing how long a race could last once interruptions were taken into account. That changed after the 2011 Canadian Grand Prix.

Heavy rain stopped the race in Montreal for around two hours. Jenson Button eventually won after a spectacular comeback drive. The official race time was 4:04:39.537, making it the longest race in Formula 1 history.

The FIA responded quickly. From 2012, a race including interruptions could last no more than four hours. The two-hour limit on actual racing remained in place. For the 2021 season, the overall limit was reduced to three hours.
Belgium 2021: The shortest race and new points rules

Formula 1 experienced the opposite extreme at Spa-Francorchamps in 2021. Persistent rain meant the field only circulated behind the Safety Car. Just one lap was included in the official classification.
Under the rules in force at the time, half points were nevertheless awarded. That prompted widespread criticism.
Since 2022, a sliding scale has therefore applied to points awarded for shortened races, provided that at least two laps have been completed without the Safety Car or Virtual Safety Car:
Two laps to 25 per cent of the race distance: points for the top five (6-4-3-2-1).
25 to 50 per cent: points for the top nine (13-10-8-6-5-4-3-2-1).
50 to 75 per cent: points for the top 10 (19-14-12-9-8-6-5-3-2-1).
Since 2023, full points have also been awarded when a suspended race is resumed, even if the full scheduled distance is ultimately not completed.
Selected race weekends also feature a Sprint alongside the Grand Prix. It covers around 100 kilometres, roughly one-third of the distance of a normal race, and usually lasts around half an hour.

There is no mandatory pit stop. Points are awarded to the top eight finishers (8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1). Six Sprints feature on the 2026 calendar. Full details of the format can be found in Formula 1 Sprint: Everything you need to know.
From 2027, the standard race distance is set to fall from 305 to 290 kilometres. According to the FIA, that equates to around two or three fewer laps.
The Formula 1 Commission has approved the reduction, although it still requires final approval from the FIA World Motor Sport Council.
Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Lando Norris, McLaren

At the same time, the current three-hour overall limit for races affected by interruptions is set to be abolished. Instead, a fixed hard stop will be introduced for the end of racing activity. The two-hour limit on actual racing time will remain.

1971年最大比赛距离从400公里降至约322公里；1989年确立305公里最低标准。
2011年加拿大站因大雨中断约两小时，官方用时4:04:39.537，成为F1史上最长比赛；此后引入总时长限制，2021年缩减为三小时。

items.summaryEn: Charles Leclerc revealed on F1's Beyond the Grid podcast that he received approaches from rival teams before signing a new Ferrari deal, but he remains coy about which teams they were.
detailZh: 夏尔·勒克莱尔在签署新法拉利合同之前，有哪些“其他机会”？
勒克莱尔谈到曾收到对手车队的接触邀请，但对这些车队究竟是谁仍保持含糊其辞。
每当法拉利和勒克莱尔同意延长双方的关系时，这条消息总是伴随着各种暗示，说勒克莱尔曾拒绝其他追求者，只为留在他真心所爱的车队。
“为此，我也很幸运能处在有经纪人帮我把关的位置上，”在F1官方播客《Beyond the Grid》最近一期节目中，当被问及他有多认真地考虑过离开法拉利的生活时，他这样说道。
“而且我的经纪人来到这里，是为了让我了解还有哪些其他机会，以及周围正在发生什么。所以我没有进行任何个人谈话，但我的经纪人谈了。”
“说实话，他的职责就是对我坦诚，向我完整呈现围场里正在发生的事情，以及我们可能有哪些机会。所以，是的，确实有其他机会。但最终，我们和法拉利坐下来谈，并且很快就达成了协议。”

如果说勒克莱尔与法拉利有着特殊的关系，那么他的经纪人托德也是如此：他是让的儿子，让曾是一名拉力赛领航员，先是主导了标致的拉力赛和耐力赛项目，随后在迈克尔·舒马赫时代带领法拉利走向世界霸主地位，之后转型进入政界，担任国际汽联主席十余年。小托德还长期管理着法拉利车手费利佩·马萨，并且至今仍负责詹姆斯·卡拉多的事务，后者曾随这支车队夺得勒芒冠军。他旗下拥有众多处于职业生涯不同阶段的车手，是围场中一位非常老练的操盘手。
但小托德在法拉利所享受到的、比其他任何地方都要多的，是能够直接与那些比车队领队更高层级的有影响力人物对话的机会——尽管他也是弗雷德里克·瓦塞尔的重要盟友，两人早在二十多年前就共同创立了ART GP车队。事实上，据悉托德在2023年1月促成前车队领队马蒂亚·比诺托下台、由瓦塞尔接任一事中发挥了关键作用。
勒克莱尔的经纪人尼古拉·托德（左）与法拉利车队领队弗雷德里克·瓦塞尔有着长期的职业合作关系。
拥有这样一位深度打入权力高层的经纪人，让勒克莱尔能够以“看似与自己无关”的方式得到他想要的东西，比如比诺托的下台——当时法拉利的复苏轨迹正出现重大摇摆——以及2024赛季初以颇为奇怪的方式将泽维尔·马尔科斯从勒克莱尔的比赛工程师位置上撤换。如果他转投另一支车队，就不会有这么大的影响力了。
同样，他的影响力不仅取决于自己的表现，还取决于他的市场价值。如果我们Motorsport.com意大利版的同行罗伯托·钦切罗所说的那样，法拉利已经把勒克莱尔锁进了一份合同“金色牢笼”里，那么以转投他队相威胁就不再是他可以打出的筹码了。
没有人怀疑勒克莱尔的速度或投入程度。可以说，他常常投入过度，尤其是在赛车不够好的时候。如果法拉利的赛车只达到领先赛车的90%或95%，夏尔就会试图用自己的方式、以冒险的形式来弥补差距。这就是为什么车迷（tifosi）们把他与吉尔·维尔纽夫放在心中同样崇高的位置。
在最近几个赛季中，勒克莱尔在法拉利之外的主要选择包括梅赛德斯、红牛和迈凯伦，这些车队的领军人物不得不权衡勒克莱尔能带来的性能收益，以及他的到来会打破车队内部平衡的问题。过去几年，尼古拉·托德肯定一直在频繁走访这些车队，但F1媒体往往在看到一名车手的经纪人出现在别家车队的房车里时就显得过于激动。
有时候，一次随意的闲聊就只是一次随意的闲聊。有时候，一笔交易可能确实正在进行中，尽管这种事情公开进行的可能性相当低。很多时候，这类会面被刻意安排在公开场合，纯粹是为了满足各方的议程：对车队领队来说，是为了向自己的车手表明他们手头还有其他选择；对经纪人来说，是为了表明他的客户在别处也受到了追捧。
今年，随着汉密尔顿推动法拉利支持他冲击世界冠军，勒克莱尔与汉密尔顿之间的关系开始变得紧张。
为了在2024年1月宣布刘易斯·汉密尔顿将于下赛季加盟时维持车队内部的平衡，法拉利同时也与勒克莱尔签下了一份长期合同，理论上附带选项可延续到2029年底，但据悉合同中还包含2026年的一个解约节点。就勒克莱尔而言，这是为了应对法拉利可能把新技术规则搞砸的情况。
相反，一幅更复杂的图景浮现出来：法拉利打造出了一辆有竞争力的赛车，并且能够通过升级为其增加性能——这在最近几年的过去并不总是如此。但它也在运作上出现了失误，错失了多次拿到更多积分的机会。
不过，其他领先车队中的局势也发生了变化。当勒克莱尔在2024年签下长期合同时，部分原因是托德知道汉密尔顿的转会即将到来，并曾接洽梅赛德斯，希望查尔斯能填补那个空缺。但当本赛季初解约条款进入视野时，梅赛德斯对当时的车手阵容非常满意。
迈凯伦也可以说同样的情况，据悉托德也与包括安德烈亚·斯特拉和扎克·布朗在内的领导层断断续续地进行过会谈。当托德在去年赛季末四处接洽时，迈凯伦有两名车手在争夺世界冠军。
据悉，阿斯顿·马丁也在去年年底发出了邀请，但那正值这支命运多舛的组织再度表现不佳、内部争斗不断的时候——新上任的技术管理合伙人阿德里安·纽维刚刚让董事总经理兼车队领队安迪·考威尔下台。在法拉利和一团糟之间做选择，勒克莱尔明智地选了第一扇门。
"我不想放弃我的终极目标，那就是和法拉利一起成为世界冠军，"勒克莱尔说。
"而且我相信这个项目。我相信车队的每一个人。
"我认为我们正处在一个不断展现创新的年份。我们在生产计划和带来的升级方面也非常激进。这让我对未来充满希望。
"而且瓦塞尔也是我再次续约的重要原因。我对瓦塞尔有百分之两百的信任。"
等下次他的合同需要续签时，勒克莱尔将年过30岁。到那时他还会像现在这样拥有这么多其他机会吗？
detailEn: What were Charles Leclerc's "other opportunities" before signing new Ferrari deal?
Charles Leclerc has spoken about receiving approaches from rival teams but remains coy about who they might actually be
Every time Ferrari and Charles Leclerc agree to extend their relationship, the news comes against a background of allusions to other suitors Charles has spurned to remain with his true love.

"For that, I'm also lucky to be in the position where I've got my manager," he said on a recent episode of F1's Beyond the Grid podcast when asked how seriously he had considered a life away from Ferrari.
"And my manager is here to let me know about what are the other opportunities, what's going on around. And so I didn't have any personal talks, but my manager did.

"I mean, it's his job to be honest with me and to give me the full picture of what's going on in the paddock and what opportunities we might have. So, yes, there were other opportunities. But at the end of the day, we sat down with Ferrari and we made it happen quite quickly."

If Leclerc has a special relationship with Ferrari, the same can be said of his manager, Todt: son of Jean, the former rally co-driver who masterminded Peugeot's rally and endurance programmes before leading Ferrari to world domination in the Michael Schumacher era, then shifted into politics as FIA president for over a decade. Todt Jr also managed long-time Ferrari driver Felipe Massa and still superintends the affairs of James Calado, a Le Mans winner with the Scuderia. He has a great many drivers on his books at all stages of the career ladder, and is a consummate player in the paddock.

But what Todt Jr enjoys to a greater extent at Ferrari than anywhere else is the ear of influential figures further up the food chain than the team principal – although he is a key ally of Frederic Vasseur, having co-founded the ART GP organisation with him over two decades ago. Indeed, it's understood that Todt was instrumental in the removal of former team principal Mattia Binotto and his replacement by Vasseur in January 2023.
Leclerc's manager Nicolas Todt (left) has a long professional relationship with Ferrari team boss Frederic Vasseur

Having a manager so plugged into the senior echelons of power enables Leclerc to get what he wants with plausible deniability, such as Binotto's departure at a time when Ferrari's recovery trajectory underwent a major wobble, and the peculiarly communicated removal of Xavier Marcos as Leclerc's race engineer early in the 2024 season. He would not have quite the same influence if he were to shift to another team.

Equally, his influence depends not just on his performance but also his market value. If Ferrari has Leclerc locked into a contractual "golden prison", as our Motorsport.com Italy colleague Roberto Chinchero puts it, then threatening to go elsewhere is no longer a lever he can pull.

Nobody doubts Leclerc's speed or commitment. Arguably he often over-commits, especially if the car isn't good enough. If the Ferrari is only 90% or 95% as good as the frontrunning car, Charles will try to make up the shortfall himself in the form of risk. That's why the Tifosi place him in the same rarefied space in their hearts as Gilles Villeneuve.

In recent seasons Leclerc's prime options outside Ferrari have been with Mercedes, Red Bull and McLaren, whose leaders have had to weigh up the performance benefits Leclerc would bring against the change in equilibrium it would cause. Nicolas Todt has certainly been busy doing the rounds of those teams over the past couple of years, but there is a tendency in the F1 media to get rather too excited when a driver's manager is spotted in another team's motorhome.

Sometimes a casual chat is just a casual chat. Sometimes a deal may actually be in progress, though the likelihood of this happening in plain sight is quite low. Often such encounters are staged in public purely to suit each party's agendas: for the team principal, to show their drivers they have other options on the table; for the manager, to show his client has interest from elsewhere.
Relations between Leclerc and Hamilton have come under strain this year as Hamilton has pushed Ferrari to support his world championship challenge

To manage the internal equilibrium when it announced in January 2024 that Lewis Hamilton would be joining the following season, Ferrari also signed Leclerc to a long-term deal that theoretically reached until the end of 2029 with options, but which was also understood to have included a break point in 2026. On Leclerc's side this was to cover the possibility of Ferrari making a mess of the new technical regulations.

Instead, a more complex picture has emerged in which Ferrari has engineered a competitive car, and has been able to add performance to it in the form of upgrades – which hasn't always been true in the recent past. But it has also suffered operational misfires and blown several chances to score more points.

The dynamic in the other leading teams has also changed, though. When Leclerc signed up for the long term in 2024, this was partially because Todt knew Hamilton's move was coming, and had approached Mercedes with a view to Charles filling that vacancy. But when the break clause came into view early this season, Mercedes was perfectly happy with its line-up.

The same could be said of McLaren, where Todt is also understood to have held discussions on and off with leaders including Andrea Stella and Zak Brown. When Todt was doing the rounds late last season, McLaren had two drivers in contention for the world championship.

It's also understood that Aston Martin made an approach at the end of last year, but this was at a time of yet more underperformance and internal wrangling in that benighted organisation, when recently installed managing technical partner Adrian Newey had MD and team principal Andy Cowell ousted. Given a choice between Ferrari and a farrago, Leclerc wisely chose door number one.
"I don't want to give up on my ultimate goal, which is to become a world champion with Ferrari," Leclerc said.
"And I believe in the project. I believe in every single person of the team.
"I think we are in a year where we've been showing innovation. We are very aggressive also in the production plan and in the upgrades we are bringing. And that gives me lots of hopes for the future.
"And Fred is a big reason on why I have signed again as well. I believe in Fred 200%."
Next time his contract is up for renewal, Leclerc will be over 30. Will he still have as many other opportunities then?

detailZh: F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛五大看点
巴库本周末庆祝其进入F1赛历十周年
车手们在F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛发车
本周末F1重返熟悉的地方，阿塞拜疆庆祝其进入赛历十周年。
巴库街道赛道2016年以欧洲大奖赛名义首次亮相，2017年起改称阿塞拜疆大奖赛，除受新冠疫情影响的2020赛季外每年均举办。
这条赛道曾诞生诸多难忘时刻，包括丹尼尔·里卡多2017年从第10位起步夺冠、2018年与队友马克斯·维斯塔潘的碰撞，以及2021年那场事故频发的比赛。
让我们期待本周末F1能带来更多同样的精彩，巴库将承办2026赛季第15站，在里海之滨的比赛之后仅剩八站。
阿塞拜疆于周日举行自己的纪念日，每年9月27日举行，以纪念在第二次纳戈尔诺-卡拉巴赫战争中阵亡的人。这场冲突于2020年当天爆发，持续44天，最终阿塞拜疆在争议的纳戈尔诺-卡拉巴赫地区对亚美尼亚取得“胜利”。
因此，由于这个欧亚国家在周日举行纪念活动，赛事组织方申请将大奖赛周末提前一天，最终也正是这样安排的。这意味着媒体日现在改在周三，随后周四进行一练和二练，分别于当地时间12:30和16:00开始。
周五现在进行三练和排位赛，同样是12:30和16:00开始，正赛则在周六15:00发车。这不应太多影响比赛本身的进行方式，但请务必设置提醒，以免把观看计划安排在周日！
能量部署再次成为首要议题
兰斯·斯特罗尔，阿斯顿·马丁车队，弗兰科·科拉平托，阿尔派
在一个平行宇宙里，如果2026年F1动力单元规则不是这么一团乱麻，那么阿塞拜疆大奖赛前的讨论理所当然会聚焦于更短、更轻、更灵活的新一代赛车在巴库街道赛道上会比它们笨重的地效前辈显得多么轻快和鲜活。下压力更小，加上更窄的轮胎，也会给这条赛道标志性的大直道以及尽头等待的危险刹车区增添趣味。
然而，令人烦恼的能量管理话题将成为车手反馈的关键点。
巴库的长直道会轻易在到达终点前很久就耗尽电池储备，触发降功率阶段，软件会逐步削减电力输入。直道上长时间使用的直线模式（SM）区域会缓解部分影响，但在2号弯和3号弯之间需要回收能量以进攻或防守，将影响车手应对1号弯大刹车的方式。
这是一条工程师会称之为确定性的赛道，因为通过使用电力增压可以找到圈速的区域是显而易见的。
这还可能放大驾驶风格上的微小差异，这些差异累积起来会导致队友之间出现不同的峰值速度。最后一个弯相当有挑战性，任何因滑动而损失的速度都必须重新加速——而这会从直道上的电力“预算”中扣除。
赛车升级一直是2026赛季的关键战场，竞争格局随着谁在何时安装升级而不断波动。这在车队前列一直是主要话题，因为领跑积分榜的梅赛德斯选择了与其两个最接近的对手法拉利和迈凯伦不同的策略。
后两者采取了激进的前置式方案，而梅赛德斯则倾向于安装针对特定比赛的小调整，其唯一的大升级包在5月的蒙特利尔才到来。不那么激进的策略让法拉利和迈凯伦缩小了差距，银箭在开局六场大奖赛中从杆位夺冠，随后八场中赢得四场。
然而，一旦它在10月2日至4日的马来西亚站安装下一个大升级，可能会重新确立这样的统治地位。所以这意味着巴库是梅赛德斯使用当前套件的最后一场比赛，而该套件表现仍不算太差，占据统治地位的积分榜领跑者基米·安东内利赢得了最近两场比赛。
照他目前的状态，人们不应赌这位20岁新星无法取得三连胜，他正继续轻松迈向首个冠军。安东内利领先队友乔治·拉塞尔81分，后者在上一站马德里实际上已放弃了自己的争冠机会。
去年，巴库本应给奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里一个巨大机会来扩大他的冠军领先优势。他前一赛季在阿塞拜疆夺冠，抵挡住了夏尔·勒克莱尔每一次超车尝试，并在2025年积累了领先兰多·诺里斯31分的榜首优势。马克斯·维斯塔潘又落后94分。
然而，皮亚斯特里冠军画卷的线头却散开了。在小雨和大风来袭之际的Q3撞车，使这位澳大利亚人在3号弯撞墙，排位仅列第九。情况只会更糟：皮亚斯特里抢跑，进入防熄火模式，掉到队尾，随后在6号弯撞车。压力击垮了通常镇定自若的墨尔本人，这一刻标志着冠军争夺中的权力转移。
皮亚斯特里回到阿塞拜疆时，自那以后再无胜绩，他上一次获胜是2025年荷兰大奖赛。本赛季总体上是挣扎的；较低的下压力水平和相关的部署策略对他并不特别合适，迈凯伦车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉认为皮亚斯特里因为不得不过多思考操作而损失时间。
但他此前已证明自己能在巴库表现出色，正如他2024年的胜利所示，如果他能够终结这段糟糕状态并取得头条成绩，那将是艰难12个月的恰当结局。
当然，便利的规律不会就这样发生——但在去年一切崩盘的赛道上实现逆转的想法，可能会给皮亚斯特里额外的动力去驱散2025年的阴影。
最近几场大奖赛中反复出现的话题之一是费尔南多·阿隆索的未来。在上一站西班牙，国际汽联主席穆罕默德·本·苏拉耶姆透露他曾与这位45岁车手交谈，并承诺在他阿斯顿·马丁车队处境糟糕之际帮助他。
“不会很快，”阿隆索本人在周四新闻发布会上被问及何时公布2027年计划时回答。“因为我觉得这样挺好，不是吗？”他补充道。巴库的问题是，围绕他未来的悬念是否仍会保持“挺好”，因为人们相信他的计划可能已经确定，他只是试图对F1施加一点压力。所以预计这位西班牙老将会更多抱怨2026年赛车有多糟糕，他的合同将在本赛季结束后到期。
在点名感谢了他的厨师和新闻官之后，车队的社区经理接下来会轮到吗？
但他的赛车呢？阿斯顿·马丁将在巴库带来其升级套件的最后部分，车队希望这最终能让AMR26更接近重量限制。本田在升级方面已无后续计划，但相信其当前套件仍有性能可挖掘，帮助实现一场积分完赛将取决于这家引擎供应商。
detailEn: Five things to look out for at the F1 Azerbaijan GP
Baku celebrates its 10th anniversary on the F1 calendar this weekend
Drivers take the start of the Formula One Azerbaijan Grand Prix
Formula 1 returns to familiar ground this weekend as Azerbaijan celebrates its 10th anniversary of being on the calendar.
The Baku street circuit first entered as the European Grand Prix in 2016 before running as the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017, featuring every season bar the COVID-struck 2020 campaign.
It has produced many memorable moments from Daniel Ricciardo’s mega win from 10th in 2017, his clash with team-mate Max Verstappen in 2018 or that incident-packed 2021 contest.
Let’s hope F1 is in for more of the same this weekend, as Baku hosts round 15 of the 2026 campaign with just eight left after the race next to the Caspian Sea.

Azerbaijan holds its own Remembrance Day on Sunday, which is held each year on the 27 September to honour those who died in the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War. The conflict began on that day in 2020 and lasted for 44 days, resulting in an Azerbaijan ‘triumph’ over Armenia in the disputed region of Nagorno-Karabakh.

So because the Euro-Asian country is marking it on Sunday, race organisers requested for the grand prix weekend to shift forwards by a day and that is exactly what’s ended up happening. It means media day will now take place on Wednesday, ahead of free practice one and two on Thursday, respectively starting at 12:30pm and 4pm locally.

Friday will now see final practice and qualifying, again 12:30pm and 4pm session starts, ahead of the race on Saturday with lights out at 3pm. It shouldn’t make too much difference to how the racing will play out, but make sure to set reminders so that plans aren’t made to watch it on Sunday!
Energy deployment at the top of the agenda again
Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing, Franco Colapinto, Alpine

In a parallel universe where the 2026 F1 power unit regulations aren’t such a bugger’s muddle, talk ahead of the Azerbaijan GP is quite rightly focusing on how the shorter, lighter, nimbler new-generation cars would look much more sprightly and alive around the Baku street circuit than their ponderous ground-effect predecessors. Having less downforce, along with narrower tyres, would also add spice to the track’s signature straight and the perilous braking area lying in wait at the end.
Instead, the vexatious topic of energy management will be the key point of driver feedback.

Baku’s long straight will easily deplete battery reserves long before the end, triggering the ramp-down phase as the software progressively tapers off electrical input. A long straightline mode (SM) zone on the straight will mitigate some of the effects, but the requirement to harvest energy to attack or defend between Turns 2 and 3 will affect the way drivers approach the big stop at Turn 1.
This is a track which the engineers would describe as deterministic, since the areas where lap time can be found through using the electrical boost are obvious.

It will also likely exaggerate the small differences in driving style that can add up to team-mates having different peak speeds. The final corner is quite challenging, and any speed scrubbed off by sliding will have to be re-accelerated – which comes out of the electrical ‘budget’ on the straight.

Car upgrades has been a key battleground of the 2026 campaign with the pecking order constantly fluctuating depending on who has fitted updates and when. It has been a major talking point at the front of the field, as championship leader Mercedes opted for a different strategy compared to its two nearest rivals, Ferrari and McLaren.

While the latter two went for an aggressive front-loaded approach, Mercedes preferred to fit minor, race-specific tweaks with its only major upgrade package arriving at Montreal in May. A less aggressive approach has allowed Ferrari and McLaren to close the gap, as the Silver Arrows won the opening six grands prix from pole before winning four of the last eight.

It might, however, re-establish such dominance once it fits its next major update in Malaysia on 2-4 October. So that means Baku is Mercedes’ last race with its current package, which still hasn’t fared too badly with dominant championship leader Kimi Antonelli winning the last two races.

At the way he is going, one shouldn’t bet against the 20-year-old sensation from making it three victories on the bounce as he continues to romp towards a maiden title. Antonelli holds an 81-point lead over team-mate George Russell in second, the Briton effectively conceding his title chances last time out in Madrid.

Last year, Baku was supposed to present Oscar Piastri with a huge opportunity to extend his championship lead. He'd won in Azerbaijan the previous season, soaking up every one of Charles Leclerc's attempts to make a pass, and over 2025 had accrued a 31-point lead over Lando Norris at the top of the standings. Max Verstappen was a further 94 points behind.

Instead, the threads of Piastri's championship tapestry unravelled. A Q3 crash amid the onset of drizzle and high winds contrived to guide the Australian's path into the wall at Turn 3, and put him ninth on the grid. It only got worse: Piastri jumped the start, went into an anti-stall, dropped to the back of the field, and then crashed at Turn 6. The pressure had got to the usually unflappable Melburnian, and this was the moment that marked the power shift in the title fight.

Piastri returns to Azerbaijan without a victory to his name since, his last being his 2025 Dutch GP. This season has, generally, been a struggle; the lower levels of downforce and the deployment tactics involved have not sat particularly well with him, and McLaren team principal Andrea Stella believes that Piastri is losing time through having to think too much about his inputs.

But he's proven before that he can perform brilliantly in Baku, per his '24 win, and it would be a fitting conclusion to a difficult 12 months if he could arrest that run of poor form and produce a headline result.

Of course, convenient patterns don't just happen quite like that - but the idea of a turnaround at the circuit where it all came apart last year could present Piastri with that extra smidgen of incentive to vanquish the spectre of 2025.

One of the recurring talking points from recent grands prix is the future of Fernando Alonso. In Spain last time out, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem revealed that he had spoken to the 45-year-old and had promised to help him amid a horrible time for his Aston Martin squad.

“Not soon,” Alonso himself replied when asked in Thursday’s press conference when he would reveal his plans for 2027. “Because I think it’s nice, no?” he added. The question in Baku is whether the intrigue surrounding his future will remain nice with the belief that his plans may already be decided and that he is simply trying to apply a little pressure on F1. So expect more complaints about just how bad the 2026 cars are from the veteran Spaniard, whose contract expires at the end of this campaign.
After name-checking his chef and his press officer, will the team’s community manager get a turn next?

But what about his car? Aston Martin is bringing the final part of its upgrade package to Baku, with the team hoping it will finally get closer to the AMR26’s weight limit. Honda, which has no more upgrades in the pipeline, believes there is still some performance to unlock from its current package, and it will be down to the engine supplier to help make a points-scoring race possible.
